transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-19 16:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Reyes (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Anil Gupta (Northstar CTO), Maya Liu (Northstar ML Eng), Priya Sharma (Northstar Platform), Liam O'Connor (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jamie from Redwood, and with me are Sofia and Ethan. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Anil Gupta: Good, thanks. Running on schedule. We wanted to dig into model selection and how the different deployment modes would map to our security needs.
[00:14] Sofia Reyes: Great, high level we'll cover hosted, dedicated, private (VPC/on-prem), then model tradeoffs — context length, multilingual, tool-calling, and perf. But we'd love to hear your priorities first.
[00:24] Maya Liu: Sure. Quick context — Northstar builds analytics insights over customer transcript data, some PII, some regulated finance customers. Main asks: 1) support 20k-40k context for long conversation history, 2) multilingual across English/French/German/Japanese, 3) tool-calling to our internal search and CRM APIs, 4) strict data residency and audit logs.
[00:45] Priya Sharma: And ops side — we need VPC peering or an on-prem option for certain customers. We prefer customer-managed KMS, granular RBAC, and traceability for token-level cost if possible.
[00:58] Jamie Park: That's super helpful. Sounds like security and long-context are primary. Quick question on scale — Liam, how many concurrent inference streams do you expect at peak?
[01:06] Liam O'Connor: For pilot maybe 50 concurrent, production target 500-800. Latency SLOs: sub-400ms for short queries, but for long-context retrieval flows we can accept higher as long as throughput is stable.
[01:20] Ethan Cole: Two axes to think about — latency/throughput and cost. Hosted is fastest to get started but has less isolation; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput; Private gives you the isolation and KMS but requires more ops. For your KMS requirement we support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated in most configs.
[01:40] Anil Gupta: For Dedicated, do we still get VPC peering? We need traffic to go through our firewall.
[01:45] Sofia Reyes: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private networking. The Private deployment is the fully customer-controlled plane and may be air-gapped if needed. Dedicated is a middle ground — reserved capacity in our infra with private connectivity options.
[01:56] Maya Liu: On models — we've been evaluating Mistral, Falcon, MPT, and some LLaMA forks. We're interested in instruction-following plus tool-calling. Thoughts on which families hit our cost/latency tradeoffs?
[02:10] Sofia Reyes: Okay, bluntly — Falcon and Mistral variants tend to be cost-effective for non-multimodal LLM inference, MPT has good instruction tuning in some forks, LLaMA derivatives vary. For tool-calling you'll want a model with structured output stability; we recommend trying a smaller instruction-tuned open model for tool orchestration and a larger model for long-context summarization if you need high quality. Also, quantization and kernel selection matter — we'll recommend int8/4-bit profiles depending on your quality targets.
[02:36] Priya Sharma: What about 32k token contexts? Is that realistic with open models on Dedicated?
[02:41] Ethan Cole: Yes, it's realistic but depends on model architecture and memory paths. We support model variants compiled for long-context and our runtime does KV cache management and continuous batching. For 32k you'll likely need higher memory GPUs or sharded execution; Dedicated pools can be configured for that. Private on-prem might be best if you want full control over hardware.
[03:02] Anil Gupta: We also need multilingual fidelity — Japanese and German are critical. Any special recommendations?
[03:07] Sofia Reyes: Models trained on multilingual corpora (Mistral mixed, some LLaMA-MT forks) perform better. Also consider instruction-tuning on your internal data for key languages. We can run a quick eval with sample prompts in EN/FR/DE/JA to surface gaps.
[03:21] Jamie Park: Real quick — tool-calling. How do you handle function calls and passing back structured JSON or vectors to our search?
[03:28] Ethan Cole: Redwood supports tool-calling patterns — streaming function call tokens, structured output enforcement, and we can surface the raw tokens plus parsed JSON. For private/Dedicated deployments you can bring your own connectors; for hosted we provide connectors and you can run middleware. Note: sometimes function-call decoding can be noisy with certain models — that's a model selection job.
[03:48] Maya Liu: Are there cadence constraints for tool-calls? We might have synchronous chat flows that call CRM and search multiple times per session.
[03:55] Sofia Reyes: You can design async tool-calling with a worker loop or do direct sync calls — if latency is a concern, we recommend batching or local caching of search vectors. Redwood Optimize can recommend caching and batching params per route.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: On cost, do you have ballpark per-token estimates for different families? We have an existing budget target per inference.
[04:18] Jamie Park: We'll send a cost matrix. Very roughly, open model on Dedicated with quantization might be X-1/3 compared to hosted larger models; we'll provide more precise in the perf doc.
[04:27] Anil Gupta: Compliance — SOC2, ISO, audit logs, SSO/SAML?
[04:32] Sofia Reyes: We are SOC2 compliant for Hosted and Dedicated control planes; Private can be in your environment with your controls. We support SAML SSO and identity federation, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. We'll attach the SOC2 report and our security brief. For KMS you can use Azure/AWS KMS or HSM if on-prem.
[04:49] Priya Sharma: How deep is observability? We need token-level cost back to a request id for billing internal teams.
[04:56] Ethan Cole: Redwood Console surfaces token-level breakdowns, per-route latency, and tracing hooks. We also expose logs you can ship to your SIEM. There are retention tiers though — if you need long retention we can add that as an add-on.
[05:09] Maya Liu: Let's talk about an experimental architecture we sketched — one model manages short query routing, another handles long-context summarization. Could Redwood support multi-model routing with fallbacks?
[05:20] Sofia Reyes: Absolutely. We have smart routing policies — route by latency or cost, fall back to cheaper variants, and can do canary rollouts. For your flow you could set a policy: short queries -> smaller model with tool-calling; heavy summarization -> long-context model with larger footprint and KV cache.
[05:36] Anil Gupta: For the pilot, we want to try Dedicated for 4 weeks with a limited pool and run benchmarks at 8k and 32k contexts. Can you run that?
[05:44] Jamie Park: Yes — typical pilot: reserved nodes for a timebox, we'll provide a benchmark plan and sample prompts. After the pilot you can decide on Dedicated expansion or move to Private.
[05:52] Liam O'Connor: Side note — we've run a small benchmarking on our infra with a LLaMA-derivative and saw tokenization hiccups; some proper nouns were mangled. Will Redwood's runtime affect tokenization?
[06:04] Ethan Cole: Tokenization is model-dependent. Our runtime doesn't alter tokenization except for normalization steps; if you see issues that's often model preproc or tokenizer mismatch. We can coordinate tokenizer versions in the benchmark.
[06:17] Maya Liu: Any gotchas with function calling and streaming? We've seen truncated JSON mid-stream when network jitter occurs.
[06:25] Sofia Reyes: We handle partial streams and can replay the last K tokens; we also support guaranteed end-of-function markers in some model configs. Network jitter should be mitigated by streaming with retry strategies. We'll include recommended SDK patterns.
[06:38] Anil Gupta: What about data residency within EU for some customers? We need models and inference to run in eu-west zones.
[06:45] Jamie Park: We have region options for Hosted and Dedicated; Private of course runs anywhere you provision. For EU residency we can pin inference to eu-west nodes and ensure data doesn't cross regions.
[06:57] Priya Sharma: One more ops question — how are upgrades and rollouts handled for Private? We run strict change windows.
[07:03] Sofia Reyes: Private gives you control — you manage the control plane or we give you a private control plane with scheduled upgrades; we support canary within your clusters so you can test on a small subset.
[07:14] Ethan Cole: Quick follow-up on model families for long-context — some Mistral derivatives have better long-context token handling, but you may need the compiled runtime for kernel optimizations. Our compile step picks kernels for attention patterns and sequence lengths.
[07:28] Maya Liu: Ok. On evaluation — we want Rouge/BLEU style metrics for summarization and some human eval for multilingual correctness. Can Redwood host evaluation harnesses?
[07:36] Sofia Reyes: We can host evals or provide the harness to run locally; we also integrate quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll run a sample eval for EN/FR/DE/JA and surface regressions.
[07:48] Anil Gupta: Final — timeline. We want a pilot in June ideally. CTO signoff in 2 weeks.
[07:55] Jamie Park: Sounds reasonable. We'll get the security packet and the perf matrix to you by Friday, and Sofia will propose benchmark dates.
[08:03] Liam O'Connor: Great. Thanks all.

Notes / rough inaccuracies: auto-ids sometimes wrong — "Liam" labelled as Speaker 3 in some parts, Valerie misheard as "Valeria" in an earlier version. A few acronyms blurred (KV cache sometimes shown as K V cache in export).
